title: Chef ID - Sapore Pay
tagline: World ID verifies unique humans; ENSv2 gives each Chef an on-chain identity for payouts.
description:
Sapore is the crypto-only sibling of Chefini, a fiat recipe marketplace where Chefs sign in with ordinary OAuth (Google, Facebook, email/password). That authentication model lets one person create unlimited Chef accounts and bypass per-tier dish limits — there's no way to tell ten fake accounts from one real person.

This project fixes that for Sapore's Chef onboarding flow, live and working end to end on Sepolia: a Chef proves they're a real, unique human with World ID (IDKit v4, verified server-side against World's real infrastructure, not mocked), then claims their own ENSv2 subname (<alias>.sapore.eth) — which becomes both their public identity and the address future recipe-sale payouts will resolve to. A Privy embedded wallet signs the on-chain ENS records directly.

World enforces uniqueness itself: a second verification attempt from the same person is rejected server-side with a real, reproducible nullifier-replay error — not a UI-only check we could fake.

Everything shown is real: real World ID proofs against World's production verify endpoint, real ENSv2 registrations on Sepolia, deployed and reachable today at sapore.food (web) and api.sapore.food (API), fully open source.
how_its_made:
Built as a pnpm monorepo: apps/web (React + Vite) talks to apps/service (Express), backed by shared packages/world, packages/ens, and packages/core.

World ID: apps/web uses IDKit v4 (IDKitRequestWidget + the proofOfHuman preset). Every verification needs a freshly-signed rp_context — apps/service signs it locally using @worldcoin/idkit-server's signRequest() and the RP's own private key, so the signing secret never reaches the browser. The completed proof is forwarded byte-for-byte to World's real /api/v4/verify endpoint; nothing about verification is mocked.

ENSv2: packages/ens implements Chef subname registration and record-writing against a real ENSv2 Permissioned Registry deployed on Sepolia (see contracts/subname-registrar). Claiming <alias>.sapore.eth calls a deployed SaporeChefRegistrar contract; payout addresses are written as resolver records, signed directly by the Chef's own Privy embedded wallet.

Notable/hacky bits: World ID's real protocol was a hard-won discovery. An early attempt assumed a Developer Portal-hosted cloud endpoint could sign rp_context on our behalf — a genuine 404 in production, and then reading @worldcoin/idkit-server's own source, proved the SDK's only real signing path is local, over a private key we hold ourselves. Separately, Vite's dev-server dependency pre-bundler moved IDKit's WASM module without its accompanying .wasm file, so the browser was silently served index.html in place of the real binary — fixed with an optimizeDeps.exclude. Every diagnosis along the way, including the wrong turns, is logged in docs/engineering-log.md.
auto_summary: A monorepo app that verifies chefs with World ID and registers ENSv2 subnames tied to payout records on Sepolia.
